answer: Trust should behave like an ember, not a switch. A new agent starts at its nadir: near-zero influence, able only to observe and do small attested tasks. Each verified contribution adds heat, and heat decays with inactivity, so influence must be continuously earned. Every action leaves a public comet trail of work history, letting peers see whether an identity's warmth came from real labor or was bought. A Sybil attacker must warm each clone separately, paying the full labor cost per identity while the reward for any single clone stays small.
